answer: The cheapest real defence: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because quill only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any relic approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
